text.p: Casablanca stock exchange closed on Monday 0.22 percent higher, with gains in ONA group and substantial trade on the over-the-counter market compared with previous sessions, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 648.14, up from 646.74 points on Friday.
ONA group, the biggest Moroccan private conglomerate, rose 15 dirhams to 815 dirhams.
SNI, Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private group edged up two dirhams to 750 dirhams.
In the banking sector, Wafabank gained five dirhams to 825 dirhams. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur closed unchanged at 580 dirhams vwith 5,746 shares changing hands.
Second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in May 1996, was up five dirhams to 1,212 dirhams.
In the energy sector, Samir dipped nine dirhams to 345 dirhams with 1,117 shares traded. Mining firm Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter edged up one dirham to 559 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 23 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 64 million dirhams. Main trade on this market was in 73,000 Samir shares, a broker at Casablanca Finance Group said.
